questions.question: Examine the role of the legal system in the novel / Saraswativijayam. What does it represent about the possibility of social change from within the existing system?
questions.solution_html:
• The legal system in Saraswativijayam functions as a key symbol of the new moral and
  • rational order introduced under British colonial rule.- It represents the emerging possibility of
  • justice and reform within a society dominated by caste discrimination and feudal oppression
  • the legal system is portrayed as an instrument of moral awakening and social correction.
  • courtroom scene, where the landlord is punished for his unjust treatment of the oppressed
  • demonstrates how the modern legal system can challenge traditional hierarchies.-Law as a
  • symbol of justice and equality- Representation of gradual social change within the system
questions.final_answer: symbol of justice and equality- Representation of gradual social change within the system
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does Kumaran Asan use contrast between purity and / impurity to critique social norms in "Chandalabhikshuki"?
questions.solution_html:
• Ananda, asks an untouchable woman for water. Society brands the girl as impure. She herself
  • believes she's polluted. The monk is considered pure and spiritual. -- Spiritual transformation
  • -- purity lies not in birth but in thought and compassion. -- Monk calls her "sister". He sees
  • beyond caste barriers. -- Girl whom society sees as impure is spiritually transformed after the
  • interaction --Lord Buddha admitted her into the order of Bhikshunis.
questions.final_answer: interaction --Lord Buddha admitted her into the order of Bhikshunis
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In the play "From the Kitchen to the Stage", how do the / neighbours and women react to the sudden stopping of the marriage?
questions.solution_html:
• Shock, confusion, and disbelief – never seen such an event at a wedding. -- Some think the
  • groom is arrested for debt – others cry out to God. -- One recalls Kunchu’s warning – calls
  • the marriage a bad idea. -- Suggest marrying the girl to Madhavan – shows shifting opinion
  • and emerging reformist thought.
